title: The refusal vocabulary
description: Closed, because a free-text reason cannot be counted, tested or gated. Claim 6's 'N proposed, M refused, K would have been wrong' exists only because the reasons are enumerable, and claim 1's 'which guardrails fired' exists for the same reason. The closed set lives in this schema; the meanings live in contracts/vocabularies/reason_codes.yaml; a test asserts the two agree in both directions. Adding a code is therefore a code change with a test, exactly as intended.

at_decision.description: A refusal of a price. No price reaches the shelf, and the safe state declared for the decision path applies instead. A refusal is a correct output, not an error.

guardrail.description: Which of the five guardrails in the envelope produces this code. `any` is for the two codes no single guardrail owns: an empty admissible range is a crossing between two of them, and a missing input can be missed by whichever rule needed it. The refusal itself always names the guardrail that actually fired.

what_would_fix_it.description: A refusal names what would fix it, even when the answer is 'nothing, and disposal is correct'.

at_design.description: A refusal before any unit is assigned. The experiment does not happen.

what_would_fix_it.description: A refusal names what would fix it. Without this the engine is an obstacle rather than a design partner.

at_readout.description: A refusal after the period closed. The experiment ran; no number may be stated from it.

check.description: Which of the four mandatory close checks produces this code.
